reason: Filtering the blood sample starts the goal of following what enters the kidney's recovery route.
expectation: I expect small substances, including some useful ones, to pass through the filter while blood cells and large proteins stay behind.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would build the urine route, but I want to follow filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose and water through along with wastes, so the recovery tube is the next part to follow.
reaction: It was interesting that filtering doesn't just remove waste.
reason: The recovery tube should show how useful substances get back into the blood.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, leaving fluid containing wastes.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would help connect the urinary organs, but I want to finish following the filtered fluid first.

effect: Useful substances and much water return to blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to continue down the tube. I can now connect the urinary organs.
reaction: The recovery step makes the filter's broad selection make more sense.
reason: The ureters provide the route from the kidneys toward the bladder.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidney outlets, leaving a connection for the bladder.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also needs connecting, but I chose to follow the route outward from the kidneys.

effect: The ureters are fitted to the kidneys; the bladder is the remaining connection.
reaction: The fitting followed the expected route.
reason: The bladder is the only offered combination and completes the route from the ureters to a storage sac.
expectation: I expect the bladder to connect to the ureters and receive fluid draining from the kidneys.

effect: The bladder is fitted, completing the route for urine to collect after traveling down the ureters.
reaction: The route from kidneys to bladder is clear.
reason: I want to follow the recovered kidney fluid through the completed urinary route.
expectation: I expect the remaining waste-containing fluid to become urine and travel toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the organs to the body also fulfills a goal, but I want to finish following the fluid first.

effect: The remaining fluid reached the bladder as urine, completing the filtering and recovery goal.
reaction: The separate blood and urine routes are clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should connect the urinary organs to the body.
expectation: I expect the kidneys, ureters and bladder to be placed in the body and connected to its blood supply.

effect: The urinary organs are connected to the body and its circulation, completing the chapter.
reaction: The final picture clearly shows both the blood supply and the route out of the body.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following filtration with recovery was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidneys take useful substances back instead of just filtering out waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder was straightforward but less interesting than following what happened to the fluid.

surprise.text: I was surprised that useful glucose and water pass through the filter along with waste and have to be recovered.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the organ fittings had a clear purpose, even when the bladder was the only offered combination.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter. Following the fluid through filtering and recovery made the kidney's job easier to understand, though the fittings were predictable.
